title: What is known about 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC---.
intro: This six-state machine is a holdout of the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on: the structure of its run (two counters ticking together), the rules proved in Lean, and the open question.
verdict: The question is open. The machine runs two binary counters off one engine, one of them with stretches of junk between its digits. It can halt only if a carry finds a 1 where it has found a 0 every time so far. No halt in the first 1011 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweeps of the run
claims.text: The shift rules the machine uses in its run (every sweep met when the symbolic simulator runs from many configurations of the run), each for every number of copies.

claims.title: Junk moves only at left-end visits
claims.text: Left-end visits come right after events 2<sup>k</sup>−2. In each of the 15 periods between visits from event 1,022 to 33,554,430, the cells that change between events are the digit cells of the right counter, at gaps of 3 cells or 3 + 7m cells (m junk units 1010000 between two digits); the layout changes from one period to the next (table in the README).

claims.title: The right counter's carry
claims.text: From the engine configuration … 0001 A> 0 0101 00 (001)k 000000 … the head carries over the k ones and comes back: r_up (5k + 13 steps) and r_down (3k + 18 steps), for every k; event0 is a whole event when the lowest digit is 0 (31 steps).

claims.title: Both counters' increments, for all sizes
claims.text: At an event (A on cell 3): the left increment with a carry over n ones (12n+24 steps), the right increment on a lowest 0 (28 steps) and with a carry over k+1 ones three cells apart (8k+36 steps), with the engine block plain or marked, and carries crossing junk units 1010000, which they leave unchanged (one unit; j units in a row, 24j+36 steps; j units and then k+1 more ones, 24j+8k+44 steps). 9 theorems.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 252 cells have been visited and 78 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct run of 1011 steps (longrun.c, the simulator of tools/c/tm.h) without a halt.

claims.title: The left side is clockwork
claims.text: Between consecutive left-end extensions the busiest cell turns exactly 2<sup>k</sup> times, each power twice (64, 64, 128, 128, ..., 2<sup>24</sup>), in the first 1.5·10<sup>9</sup> steps.

claims.title: E1 is rare
claims.text: E1 is used 306 times in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps; every other non-halting transition 10<sup>7</sup> to 2·10<sup>8</sup> times.

claims.title: Both counters go up by 1 at every event
claims.text: Over the whole period from step 108,210,236 to 153,262,400 (524,288 events, the head turning in A at the engine) the left counter read off the tape goes 0, 1, 2, ..., 2<sup>19</sup> − 1, up by exactly 1 each time (in the reference machine; this run is the same); the right counter read from its digit cells (9, 19, 22, 25, 28, 31, 34, 72, 75, 85 cells right of the head) goes up by 1 modulo 2<sup>10</sup> from one event to the next at all but 4 of the 524,287 steps, at the start of the period and where a carry reaches a digit for the first time (the digit cells are then still being rewritten).

claims.title: The same run as 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC---
claims.text: Run side by side for 10<sup>10</sup> steps, the two machines have the same head position and the same tape at every step; the states differ at 423 steps (after E1, where one is in F and the other in B, both reading a 0 and both doing 0RC).

claims.title: How much of the run the increments cover
claims.text: In the first 108 steps (1,048,574 events) 95.2% of the events are instances of these theorems (left 524,258; right0 262,133; right1 92,325; junk_10 78,635; junk_110 39,313; junk_jk 1,733; right1m 9; right0m 1). The other 50,167 are carries over junk layouts the rules do not list (two junk stretches, junk words other than 1010000) and the moments around left-end visits.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.073). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).

claims.title: Two counters of the same events
claims.text: Read off the run: the counters on the two sides of the engine both go up by 1 at every visit of the head to the engine, one of them with fixed junk stretches between some digits; the junk is written when a carry reaches the end of the tape.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts only if F reads a 1, i.e. only if after D1 (0RF) only the head finds a 1; it never has, and the layout of the junk, which would decide it, is not decoded.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same tape and head as 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- at every one of the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the tables differ). The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 4 other holdouts (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine builds two binary counters that tick together, one on each side of an engine. The left one runs with clockwork regularity; the right one has stretches of junk between its digits, and that is where the open question lives. It would halt only if a carry ever found a 1 where it has always found a 0.

facts.text: No halt in a direct run.
Turns of the busiest cell between left-end extensions.
The sweeps of the run, proved for every length.

sections.heading: Two binary counters and junk that moves only at the left end
html: Watch the head in state A on cell 3 (counting from the start cell): an event. The tape there reads … L 0001 | p 0 1010000 R …. L is a binary counter with 4-cell digits (0001 = 0, 0101 = 1). p says which counter this event feeds: 1 for L, 0 for R. R is a binary counter with one cell per digit, lowest first, the digits three cells apart (1 00 1 00 0 = 3) — except where one or more junk units 1010000 (7 cells) are wedged between two digits.

Both increments are proved in Lean for every size, and so is the fact that a carry walks straight through a junk unit and leaves it as it was. The left counter is a clockwork: the left end is visited right after events 2, 6, 14, 30, …, 2k−2. Inside one period between two such visits the junk does not move at all: the only cells that change are the digit cells of R. Only at a left-end visit is the junk regrouped. For instance between events 65,534 and 131,070 there is one junk unit after digits 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, two after digit 9 and one after digit 11; in the next period there are three after digit 3, one after digits 4 and 5, two after 9 and one after 11 and 12.

The machine can halt only when D1 (0RF) is followed by a 1. The proved increments never do that, so a halt has to come from a moment they do not cover: a left-end visit, a right-end extension, or a carry meeting junk in an unlisted way. Decoding the regrouping rule would turn the junk layout into a function of the period number and settle where such moments can occur.

sections.heading: Two counters and an engine
html:
Most of the time the tape is L · engine · R. Each visit of the head to the engine is an event, and every event adds 1 to both counters. In the reference machine of the family (1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC---), L is written in blocks of four cells, 0101 for a 1 and 0001 for a 0, lowest digit next to the engine, and R keeps one cell per digit, three cells apart (the cells 9, 12, 15, … right of the head), lowest digit nearest the engine. Nine consecutive events of the reference machine right after its left-end visit at step 1,571,372 (the head in state A on the bold cell):

This machine is the reference machine with E1 = 1RB instead of 1RF: after E1 the head reads a 0 every time, and F0 = B0 = 0RC, so the run is the reference machine's run cell for cell (same head and tape at every step for 1010 steps).

sections.heading: The left side is clockwork
html:
When L overflows, the carry runs to the left end of the tape, the tape grows by two cells there, and L starts again. The lowest digit of L is the cell where the head turns most often, and the number of its turns between two consecutive left-end extensions follows a strict pattern, without a single exception in the first 1.5·109 steps (ymax.c):

64 64 128 128 256 256 512 512 … 223 223 224

So the periods of the left side are powers of two in events, each length twice (the counter gains one digit every two periods). The time per event is not constant, because a carry on the right costs more when it crosses junk, so the steps between left-end extensions grow by factors between about 1.35 and 2.05 instead of exactly 2.

sections.heading: A counter with junk between its digits
html: The cells that change between events are the digits of the counters: each digit changes about half as often as the one before (chg.c counts, over a whole period, how often each cell changes from one event to the next). On the right, between some digits of R, there are stretches of fixed cells (0101010101 00 1 00 1 00 1 and the like) that the carries cross without changing. They are written when a carry runs into the end of the tape, at irregular event counts, and their layout is what makes the run irregular. How they are produced is not decoded yet.

sections.heading: The dangerous moments
html: The machine halts only in state F reading a 1, and F is entered from D1 (0RF) only. After D1, used about 4·107 times in 109 steps, the head has read a 0 every time. The rare transition E1 (306 uses) leads to B here, not F; in the reference machine E1 fires when a carry of the right counter reaches a digit for the first time since the last left-end visit: right after the visit at step 2,188,604 it fires at steps 2,188,675, 2,188,767, 2,188,882, 2,189,117, 2,189,592, 2,190,547, 2,192,462, three cells further right each time and after twice the wait each time, as a binary counter reaching new digits. So this machine halts only if an ordinary carry finds a 1 after D1, while the reference machine would also halt at a fresh digit followed by a 1, where this one goes on. None of this has happened; whether the junk can ever arrange it is the open question.

sections.heading: Eight machines, one mechanism
html: The family (G11-Y): 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- (the reference), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC--- (the same run), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD0LC_0RC---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_1RB0RD_0RB---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA--- (all with left-end extensions after 2k events, each twice, to within a few hundred steps of each other); 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE--- and 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE--- (the same right part, a differently written left counter); and the mirror case 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD1RF_1LA---, with the junk on the left.

sections.heading: The same theorems for the relatives
html:
The event theorems of this machine were run on every relative. Three of them prove all nine unchanged and pass through exactly the same tapes at every event: …0RD1RF_0RC--- (E1 goes to F, which on a 0 acts as B), …0RD0LC_0RC--- (E1 takes a 5-step detour, so it runs 4 steps behind per use of E1) and 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_…_0LA--- (2 steps behind per E1). In …1RB0RD_0RB--- and the twin …0LA1RB_1RE--- one visit to the engine does both increments in one pass. 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_…_0LA0RE_1RE--- runs the same counters with other words. Only …0LA0RB_0RD1RF_1LA--- leaves: at the first use of E1, at step 87, it writes a 1 this machine never writes, and its run is a different one.

In the first 108 steps, 95.2% of this machine's 1,048,574 events are instances of the nine theorems. The rest are carries across junk shaped differently from 1010000, which appear right after a left-end visit and stay for the whole period.

sections.heading: What would settle it
html: Decode what a carry writes when it reaches the end of the tape, as a function of the counters, so that the layout of the junk after each visit is a formula. Then the question becomes whether a carry can ever find a 1 where it has always found a 0, which may be provable by an invariant of the junk, or may reduce to an arithmetic question about the two counters.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.073). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).
After 109 steps the tape spans 252 cells (88 left of the start, 153 right), with a density of 1s of 0.31.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same run as 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- (observed, not proved). At every one of the first 107 steps from blank tape the two machines have the same tape and the head on the same cell. Their tables differ, and no renaming of the states turns one into the other. While they run, the states pair up as A–A, B–B, B–F, C–C, D–D, E–E, F–F (this machine first), which is not one to one. Transitions not used in these steps: this machine never uses F1 and the other never uses F1. Lean proves (lean/Twin.lean here, lock_or_break, not_halts_of_noBreak) that the two runs have the same tape, the same head position and paired states up to the first break, a configuration where the paired states act differently, and that neither machine halts if no break ever comes. A halt of either machine is itself a break, and the halting transitions of the two do not correspond, so the two are not known to halt together.

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD0LC_0RC---: 9,999,409 configurations, the last at step 9,999,408 here and step 10,000,000 there
  • 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_1RB0RD_0RB---: 8,749,634 configurations, the last at step 9,999,093 here and step 9,999,999 there
  • 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA---: 9,999,705 configurations, the last at step 9,999,704 here and step 10,000,000 there
  • 1RB1LD_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD1RB_0LD---: 7,916,520 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 9,166,232 there

summary: Two binary counters tick together off one engine; the left one is clockwork, the right one has junk between its digits; it halts only if a carry finds a 1 where it has always found a 0 (family Y: E1 = 1RB, same run).
